titleStmt.title: Shiji 史记 · 秦庄襄王三年: introductions

div.p: The Basic Annals of Qin for the third and last year of King Zhuangxiang: Meng Ao's campaigns in Wei and Zhao, the founding of Taiyuan Commandery, the five-state army under Lord Xinling that drove Qin back to Hewai, and the king's death in May and the accession of his son Zheng.
The row of the Table of the Six States for this year: the entries for Qin, Wei and Han.

The Hereditary Houses of Chu, Zhao, Wei and Han for this year: the accession of Zhao Zheng, the exchange of six towns between Zhao and Yan, Wuji's victory at Hewai and the Wei hostage Zeng spared by Qin, and the loss of Han's Shangdang.

The second half of the Biography of the Prince of Wei, Lord Xinling: his ten years in Zhao, his return to command the five states against Qin in the thirtieth year of King Anxi, the slander that undid him, and his death; told in full under 256 BC and repeated here for the year of the victory at Hewai.

The Biography of Lü Buwei from King Zhuangxiang's death: Buwei as Chancellor of State and Second Father to the young king, his three thousand retainers and Master Lü's Spring and Autumn Annals, and the matter of Lao Ai and the Queen Dowager; and the Biography of Li Si from his birth at Shangcai to his arrival in Qin in this year, his counsel to King Zheng, the memorial against the expulsion of the guests, and his rise to Chancellor.

Ivar the Boneless' commentary on the year: the attacks of Wei, Chu and Yan on Qi, Tian Dan's siege of Liaocheng, and Chu and Wei's turn from Qi to an alliance against Qin, each with the Biographies of Lu Zhonglian and Zou Yang adduced as the probable source, their date left open; and the passage itself, Lu Zhonglian's refusal of reward and his letter to the general of Yan in Liaocheng.
Ivar the Boneless' second column: the revolt of Jinyang, which the sources put in the following year, and Wei's seizure of Han's Guan, of unknown source.
